Registers are devices that temporarily store and transfer data.
INTRODUCTIONM
A register that stores data is called a storage register. It is primarily used for temporary storage of data.
A register that transfers data is called a shift register. It is primarily used to transfer data from one circuit to another.
Let's begin the lesson on 4 BIT STORAGE REGISTER..........................
LESSON MENU
4 BIT STORAGE REGISTER
A 4 bit storage register is designed to temporarily store 4 bits of binary data.
DISCUSSION
Other registers store 8 and 16 bits. Connecting three 4 bit registers will allow storage of 12 bits of data.
The 4 bit register is used in this lesson because it is easy to understand.
Data is transferred to the register and stored as separate bits until needed.
When the register receives a command to transfer the data, the stored information is sent to the output.
The four bits of data are stored and shifted by 4 flip-flops inside the register.
The 4 bit storage register can use serial or parallel transfer. Let's look at a serial storage register first.
This serial 4 bit storage register uses four Type D edge triggered flip-flops connected to the same clock input.
The register's input is applied to the D input of the first flip-flop (A).
The output from each flip-flop is the input to the next flip-flop.
The register's output is taken from the last flip-flop (D).
Each time the clock pulse goes high, all four flip-flops change state according to their inputs.
Let's use the binary number 1011 to demonstrate how serial data is stored and transferred through a register.
Assume all flip-flops are reset and the content of the register is 0000.
During T1, the clock pulse goes high enabling all 4 flip-flops.
Flip-flop A sets. The 1 on its input is transferred into the register. The register's content is now 1000.
During T2 all 4 flip-flops are again enabled. A and B have high inputs allowing them to set.
During T3 all flip-flops are again enabled. A resets and B and C set. The register shifted the data to the right. The content is now 0110.
During T4 all flip-flops are again enabled. A, C and D set and B resets. The content of the register is now 1011.
When serial transfer is used, one clock pulse is needed to transfer each bit of data.
If the clock pulses continue, the data transfers out of the register one bit at a time. Touch NEXT and observe clock pulses T5 through T8.
1011 was shifted out one bit at a time. The register now contains 0000.
The circulate path allows the register to store data. The contents of the register are not lost when shifted to the output.c
The Circulate/Load switch, S1, selects data from the circulate (feedback) path or from the load (data input) path.
Four clock pulses will shift the registers data to the next circuit in line AND feed the data back to the register.
The next four clock pulses send the same data to the next circuit and feed the data back to the register.
Placing S1 to the LOAD position disconnects the circulate path and new data is loaded into the register.
At T0 the content of the register is 0000. What is the content of the register at T3?
The register transfers one bit in for each clock pulse. After 3 pulses only 3 bits of new data have transferred.
TRY AGAIN!
At T0 the content of the register is 0000. What is the content of the register at T3?
The register transfers one bit in for each clock pulse. After 3 pulses only 3 bits of new data have transferred.
TRY AGAIN!
At T0 the content of the register is 1111. What is the content of the register at T2?
The register transfers one bit in for each clock pulse. After 2 pulses only 2 bits of new data have transferred.
TRY AGAIN!
Next, let's look at a parallel storage register............
This parallel 4 bit storage register uses four Type D edge triggered flip-flops connected to the same clock input.
The register has a separate input applied to each flip-flop's D input.
These separate inputs allow 4 bits of data to enter into the register on each clock pulse.
A separate output is taken from each flip-flop's Q output.m
These separate outputs allow 4 bits of data to leave the register on each clock pulse.
Each time the clock pulse goes high, all four flip-flops change state according to their input.
Assume all flip-flops are reset and the contents of the register is 0000.
Let's use the binary number 1011 to demonstrate how data is stored and transferred through a 4 bit parallel register.
When the clock goes high, each flip-flop is enabled. Any data on the input is transferred to the register and to the output.
When parallel transfer is used, only one clock pulse is needed to transfer all 4 bits of data.
At T0 the content of the register is 0000. What is the content of the register at T1?
All bits are transferred to the register on each clock pulse. After one pulse all new data is transferred.
TRY AGAIN!
At T0 the content of the register is 1111. What is the content of the register at T1?
All bits are transferred to the register on each clock pulse. After one pulse all new data is transferred.
TRY AGAIN!
This completes the information on 4 BIT STORAGE REGISTER...
1. The 4 bit storage register is designed to temporarily store four bits of data.
2. A serial register transfers one bit in or out for each clock pulse.
3. In a serial storage register, circulate is used so that the data is stored when the data is shifted out.
4. A parallel register transfers all bits on one clock pulse. The outputs are always available.
